## Appendix A Optimal controller for LQR tracking problem

We derive in this section the optimal controller for the cost $J$ in Equation (1). We will show that the optimal controller takes the form $u_{t}=Kx_{t}+\tilde{K}x^{*}$ .

#### Proposition 4 (Optimal controller for $J$ ).

Suppose the system given by $(A,B)$ is controllable. The cost-to-go value function, $V(x_{0})$ , for the discounted infinite-horizon problem 1, takes the form

$$ \displaystyle V(x_{0})=x_{0}^{\top}Px_{0}+2x_{0}^{\top}q+r, $$

where

$$ \displaystyle P=Q-(\gamma B^{\top}PA)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}PA)+\gamma A^{\top}PA, \displaystyle q=-(I-\gamma(A+BK)^{\top})^{-1}Qx^{*}, \displaystyle r=\frac{1}{1-\gamma}\left((x^{*})^{\top}Qx^{*}-(\gamma B^{\top}q)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}q)\right). $$

Moreover, the optimal controller is time-invariant and of the form

$$ \displaystyle u=Kx+\tilde{K}x^{*},where $$

$$ K=-(R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}PA),\quad\tilde{K}=-(R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}\gamma B^{\top}(I-\gamma(A+BK)^{\top})^{-1}Q. $$

Then, this same controller is also the optimal policy to minimize the expected cost $J$ (where expectation is taken over the initial state $x_{0}$ ). The optimal expected cost takes the following form

$$ \displaystyle J^{\mathrm{opt}} \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[x_{0}^{\top}Px_{0}+2x_{0}^{\top}q+r]=\tr(P\Sigma)+2\mathbb{E}[x_{0}]^{\top}q+r, $$

where $\Sigma=\mathbb{E}[x_{0}x_{0}^{\top}]$ .

#### Proof.

We note that the cost-to-go value function starting from $x_{0}$ takes the form

$$ V(x_{0})=x_{0}^{\top}Px_{0}+2x_{0}^{\top}q+r, $$

which is motivated by appealing to the value function in the finite horizon [1] and taking the limit as $t$ goes to infinity.

Then,

$$ \displaystyle V(x)=\min_{u}(x-x^{*})^{\top}Q(x-x^{*})+u^{\top}Ru+\gamma V(Ax+Bu). $$

Taking the gradient with respect to $u$ , we find that

$$ \displaystyle\nabla_{u} \displaystyle=2Ru+\nabla_{u}(\gamma\left((Ax+Bu)^{\top}P(Ax+Bu)+2(Ax+Bu)^{\top}q+r\right)) \displaystyle=2Ru+2\gamma B^{\top}P(Ax+Bu)+2\gamma B^{\top}q. $$

Setting $\nabla_{u}$ to be 0, we find that $2(R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)u+2\gamma B^{\top}PAx+2\gamma B^{\top}q=0$ , which implies that

$$ \displaystyle u^{*}=-(R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}PAx+\gamma B^{\top}q). $$

Then, plugging this back into $V(x)$ ,

$$ \displaystyle V(x) \displaystyle=x^{\top}Qx+2x^{\top}(-Qx^{*})+(x^{*})^{\top}Qx^{*} \displaystyle\quad+\left((R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}PAx+\gamma B^{\top}q)\right)^{\top}R\left((R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}PAx+\gamma B^{\top}q)\right) \displaystyle\quad+\gamma[(Ax-B\left((R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}PAx+\gamma B^{\top}q)\right))^{\top}P \displaystyle\quad\quad(Ax-B\left((R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}PAx+\gamma B^{\top}q)\right))^{\top}] \displaystyle\quad+\gamma\left(2q^{\top}(Ax-B\left((R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}PAx+\gamma B^{\top}q)\right))\right)+\gamma r \displaystyle=x^{\top}Qx+2x^{\top}(-Qx^{*})+(x^{*})^{\top}Qx^{*} \displaystyle\quad+(\gamma B^{\top}PAx+\gamma B^{\top}q)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}PAx+\gamma B^{\top}q) \displaystyle\quad-\gamma\left[2(Ax)^{\top}P(B\left((R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}PAx+\gamma B^{\top}q)\right))\right] \displaystyle\quad+\gamma x^{\top}A^{\top}PAx \displaystyle\quad+2\gamma\left[q^{\top}Ax-q^{\top}(B\left((R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}PAx+\gamma B^{\top}q)\right))\right]+\gamma r \displaystyle=x^{\top}Qx+2x^{\top}(-Qx^{*})+(x^{*})^{\top}Qx^{*} \displaystyle\quad-(\gamma B^{\top}PAx+\gamma B^{\top}q)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}PAx+\gamma B^{\top}q) \displaystyle\quad+\gamma x^{\top}A^{\top}PAx+2\gamma q^{\top}Ax+\gamma r $$

Collecting terms, we find that

$$ \displaystyle P=Q-(\gamma B^{\top}PA)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}PA)+\gamma A^{\top}PA, \displaystyle q=-Qx^{*}-(\gamma B^{\top}PA)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}q)+\gamma A^{\top}q, \displaystyle r=\frac{1}{1-\gamma}\left((x^{*})^{\top}Qx^{*}-(\gamma B^{\top}q)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}PB)^{-1}(\gamma B^{\top}q)\right). $$

Finally, observe that after rearranging the equation involving $q$ ,

$$ \displaystyle q=-(I-\gamma(A+BK)^{\top})^{-1}Qx^{*}. $$

Plugging this back into the optimal formula for $u^{*}$ then yields our desired result for the case with fixed $x_{0}$ . Since the optimal controller is independent of the initial state $x_{0}$ , and the stochasticity in the population cost $J$ is over the initial state $x_{0}$ , this shows that the same controller is optimal in minimizing $J$ . ∎

## Appendix B Properties of LQR tracking

### B.1 Non-convexity

We provide here a simple example, $n=2$ ( here $n$ is state dimension), showing that $J(K)$ , the zero-target LQR cost, is non-convex. By extension $J(K,\tilde{K})$ cannot be convex in general as well.

#### Proposition 5.

Consider the zero-target LQR cost

$$ J(K)=\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}x_{t}^{\top}Qx_{t}+u_{t}^{\top}Ru_{t}, $$

where $u_{t}=Kx_{t}$ , and $x_{t+1}=Ax_{t}+Bu_{t}$ , where $x_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ and $u_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{k}$ . Then $J(K)$ is in general non-convex for $n\geq 2$ .

#### Proof.

We provide a counterexample where the set of stable controllers $K$ is not convex. Pick

$$ A=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\
0&1\end{bmatrix},\quad B=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\
0&1\end{bmatrix},\quad K_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-1.5&4042\\
0&-1.5\end{bmatrix},\quad K_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-1.5&0\\
4040&-1.5\end{bmatrix}. $$

Then, $(A,B)$ is a controllable system. In addition, observe that

$$ \rho(A+BK_{1})=\rho\left(\begin{bmatrix}-0.5&4042\\
0&-0.5\end{bmatrix}\right)<1,\quad\rho(A+BK_{2})=\rho\left(\begin{bmatrix}-0.5&0\\
4042&-0.5\end{bmatrix}\right)<1. $$

However,

$$ \rho\left(A+B\left(\frac{K_{1}+K_{2}}{2}\right)\right)=\rho\left(\begin{bmatrix}-0.5&2021\\
2021&-0.5\end{bmatrix}\right)>1, $$

which can be shown via direct computation. This proves that LQR is in general non-convex for $n\geq 2$ . ∎

### B.2 Gradient dominance

In this subsection, we fill in the gaps in our earlier proof sketch of Proposition 1. We denote $g:=\tilde{K}x^{*}$ . For notational convenience, we interchangeably refer to a policy given by $u_{t}=Kx_{t}+\tilde{K}x^{*}$ as $(K,g)$ or $(K,\tilde{K})$ . The corresponding cost-to-go-function is $V_{K,\tilde{K}}:=V_{K,g}:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ , where for any $z\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle V_{K,\tilde{K}}(z):=V_{K,g}(z)=\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}c(x_{t},Kx_{t}+g),\quad\mbox{where }x_{0}=z. $$

We now state and prove a lemma describing the value function of $J$ that we required in the proof sketch of Proposition 1.

#### Lemma 4 (Value function of $J$ ).

Suppose $\sqrt{\gamma}\rho((A+BK))<1$ . Define $g:=\tilde{K}x^{*}$ . Then,

$$ \displaystyle V_{K,\tilde{K}}(z):=V_{K,g}(z)=z^{\top}P_{K}z+2z^{\top}q_{K,g}+r_{K,g}, $$

where

$$ \displaystyle P_{K}=Q+K^{\top}RK+\gamma(A+BK)^{\top}P_{K}(A+BK), \displaystyle q_{K,g}=(I-\gamma(A+BK)^{\top})^{-1}\left(-Qx^{*}+K^{\top}Rg+\gamma(A+BK)^{\top}P_{K}Bg\right), \displaystyle r_{K,g}=\frac{1}{1-\gamma}\left((x^{*})^{\top}Qx^{*}+g^{\top}Rg+\gamma\left(g^{\top}B^{\top}P_{K}Bg+2g^{\top}B^{\top}q_{K,g}\right)\right), $$

and we can also rewrite $q_{K,g}$ as $q_{K,g}:=q_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}$ , where

$$ \displaystyle q_{K,\tilde{K}}=(I-\gamma(A+BK)^{\top})^{-1}\left(-Q+K^{\top}R\tilde{K}+\gamma(A+BK)^{\top}P_{K}B\tilde{K}\right). $$

#### Proof.

We note that direct calculations show that $V_{K,g}(z)=z^{\top}P_{K}z+2z^{\top}q_{K,g}+r$ for some $P_{K},q_{K,g},$ and $r_{K,g}$ . We will seek to find a recursive formula for $P_{K},q_{K,g}$ and $r_{K,g}$ . Since $V_{K,g}(z)=z^{\top}P_{K}z+2z^{\top}q_{K,g}+r_{K,g}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle V_{K,g}(z) \displaystyle=z^{\top}P_{K}z+2z^{\top}q_{K,g}+r_{K,g} \displaystyle=c(z,Kz+g)+\gamma V_{K,g}(Az+B(Kz+g)) \displaystyle=(z-x^{*})^{\top}Q(z-x^{*})+(Kz+g)^{\top}R(Kz+g) \displaystyle\quad+\gamma(A+BK)z+Bg)^{\top}P_{K}((A+BK)z+Bg)+2((A+BK)z+Bg)^{\top}q_{K,g}+r_{K,g} \displaystyle=z^{\top}(Q+K^{\top}RK+(A+BK)^{\top}P_{K}(A+BK))z \displaystyle\quad+2z^{\top}(-Qx^{*}+K^{\top}Rg+(A+BK)^{\top}P_{K}Bg+(A+BK)^{\top}q_{K,g}) \displaystyle\quad+(x^{*})^{\top}x^{*}+g^{\top}Rg+\gamma g^{\top}B^{\top}P_{K}Bg+2g^{\top}B^{\top}q_{K,g}+r_{K,g}. $$

Matching coeffients, we find that

$$ \displaystyle P_{K}=Q+K^{\top}RK+\gamma(A+BK)^{\top}P_{K}(A+BK), \displaystyle q_{K,g}=-Qx^{*}+K^{\top}Rg+\gamma(A+BK)^{\top}P_{K}Bg+\gamma(A+BK)^{\top}q_{K,g}, \displaystyle r_{K,g}=(x^{*})^{\top}Qx^{*}+g^{\top}Rg+\gamma\left[g^{\top}B^{\top}P_{K}Bg+2g^{\top}B^{\top}q_{K,g}+r_{K,g}\right]. $$

Some algebraic simplifications for the equations involving $q_{K,g}$ and $r_{K,g}$ then yield the result. ∎

Next we compute $\nabla J$ , which we also used in proving Proposition 1.

#### Lemma 5.

Define

$$ C_{K}=RK+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}(BK+A),\quad d_{K,\tilde{K}}=R\tilde{K}+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B\tilde{K}+\gamma B^{\top}q_{K,\tilde{K}}. $$

The gradients of $J$ with respect to $K$ and $\tilde{K}$ are the following:

$$ \displaystyle\nabla_{K}J=2C_{K}\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}+2d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}^{\top},\quad\nabla_{\tilde{K}}J=\left(2C_{K}\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}+2\beta_{\gamma}d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\right)(x^{*})^{\top}, $$

where

$$ \displaystyle\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}:=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}x_{t}x_{t}^{\top}\right],\quad\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}:=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}x_{t}\right],\quad\beta_{\gamma}:=\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}. $$

#### Proof.

Observe that for any $z\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle V_{K,g}(z) \displaystyle=c(z,Kz+g)+\gamma V((A+BK)z+Bg) \displaystyle=(z-x^{*})^{\top}Q(z-x^{*})+(Kz+g)^{\top}R(Kz+g) \displaystyle\quad+\gamma\left(((A+BK)z+Bg)^{\top}P_{K}((A+BK)z+Bg)+2((A+BK)z+Bg)^{\top}q_{K,g}+r_{K,g}\right). $$

Taking the gradient first with respect to $K$ , using the product rule we find that

$$ \displaystyle\nabla_{K}V_{K,g}(z) \displaystyle=2R(Kz+g)z^{\top}+2\gamma\left(B^{\top}P_{K}((A+BK)z+Bg)z^{\top}+B^{\top}q_{K,g}z^{\top}\right) \displaystyle\quad+\gamma\nabla_{K}V_{K,g}(x_{1})\big|_{x_{1}=(A+BK)z+Bg}. $$

Using recursion, and taking expectations, we find that

$$ \displaystyle\nabla_{K}J \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}2\gamma^{t}\left((RK+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}(A+BK))x_{t}x_{t}^{\top}+(Rg+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}Bg+B^{\top}q_{K,g})x_{t}^{\top}\right)\right] $$

We next compute the gradient with respect to $g$ . Observe that

$$ \displaystyle\nabla_{g}V_{K,g}(z) \displaystyle=2R(Kz+g)+2\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}((A+BK)z+Bg)+2\gamma B^{\top}q_{K,g}+\gamma\nabla_{g}V(x_{1})\big|_{x_{1}=(A+BK)z+Bg}. $$

Using recursion, and taking expectations, we find that

$$ \displaystyle\nabla_{g}J \displaystyle=2\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\left((RK+\gamma B^{\top}P(A+BK))x_{t}+Rg+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}Bg+\gamma B^{\top}q_{K,g}\right)\right]. $$

Since $g=\tilde{K}x^{*}$ , it follows then that

$$ \displaystyle\nabla_{\tilde{K}}J \displaystyle=2\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\left((RK+\gamma B^{\top}P(A+BK))x_{t}+Rg+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}Bg+\gamma B^{\top}q_{K,g}\right)\right](x^{*})^{\top}. $$

∎

We define the advantage function $A_{K,g}(x,u)$ as

$$ \displaystyle A_{K,g}(x,u):=c(x,u)+\gamma V_{K,g}(Ax+Bu)-V_{K,g}(x). $$

For any two policies $(K,g)$ and $(K^{\prime},g^{\prime})$ , the next lemma provides an expression for the difference between $J(K,g)$ and $J(K^{\prime},g^{\prime})$ in terms of the advantage function. This played a key role in the proof sketch of Proposition 1.

Note that any two policies $(K,\tilde{K})$ and $(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})$ correspond to policies $(K,g)$ and $(K,g^{\prime})$ , where $u_{t}=Kx_{t}+g$ and $u_{t}^{\prime}=K^{\prime}x_{t}^{\prime}+g^{\prime}$ , and $g=\tilde{K}x^{*},g^{\prime}=\tilde{K}^{\prime}x^{*}$ . \displaystyle=2\tr((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(RK+B^{\top}P_{K}(BK+A))xx^{\top}) \displaystyle\quad+2\tr((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(Rg+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}Bg+\gamma B^{\top}q_{K,g})x^{\top}) \displaystyle\quad+2\tr((g^{\prime}-g)^{\top}((RK+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}(A+BK))x+Rg\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}Bg+\gamma B^{\top}q_{K,g}) \displaystyle\quad+2\tr((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(g^{\prime}-g)x^{\top}) \displaystyle\quad+\tr(xx^{\top}(K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(K^{\prime}-K))+(g^{\prime}-g)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(g^{\prime}-g) \displaystyle=2\tr((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(C_{K}x+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})x^{\top})+2\tr((g^{\prime}-g)^{\top}(C_{K}x+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})) \displaystyle\quad+2\tr((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(g^{\prime}-g)x^{\top}) \displaystyle\quad+\tr(xx^{\top}(K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(K^{\prime}-K))+(g^{\prime}-g)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(g^{\prime}-g) $$

Above, (B.2) holds by plugging in the expression for $V_{K,g}(x)$ in Line (11). For the last line, we defined

$$ C_{K}:=RK+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}(BK+A),\quad d_{K,\tilde{K}}:=R\tilde{K}+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B\tilde{K}+\gamma B^{\top}q_{K,\tilde{K}}. $$

Completing the square, using the fact that $(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)$ is positive definite, we find that the advantage function satisfies the following inequality:

$$ \displaystyle A_{K,g}(x,K^{\prime}x+g^{\prime}) \displaystyle=\left((K^{\prime}-K)x+(g^{\prime}-g)+(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)^{-1}\left(C_{K}x+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\right)\right)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B) \displaystyle\quad\left((K^{\prime}-K)x+(g^{\prime}-g)+(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)^{-1}\left(C_{K}x+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\right)\right) \displaystyle\quad-(C_{K}x+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)^{-1}(C_{K}x+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}) \displaystyle\geq-(C_{K}x+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)^{-1}(C_{K}x+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}) $$

Using (13), and taking expectations, we find that

$$ \displaystyle J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})-J(K,\tilde{K}) \displaystyle\geq-\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\left((C_{K}x_{t}^{\prime}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)^{-1}(C_{K}x_{t}^{\prime}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})\right)\right]. $$

Applying this to an optimal policy $(K^{\mathrm{opt}},\tilde{K}^{\mathrm{opt}})$ , we find that

$$ \displaystyle J(K,\tilde{K})-J(K^{\mathrm{opt}},\tilde{K}^{\mathrm{opt}}) \displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\left((C_{K}x_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)^{-1}(C_{K}x_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})\right)\right] \displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{\sigma_{\min}(R)}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\left((C_{K}x_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})^{\top}(C_{K}x_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})\right)\right] \displaystyle=\frac{1}{\sigma_{\min}(R)}\left(\tr\left(C_{K}^{\top}C_{K}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}x_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}}(x_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}})^{\top}\right]\right)+2\tr\left(\left(\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}x_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}}\right]\right)^{\top}C_{K}^{\top}d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\right)+\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\left\lVert d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\right\rVert^{2}\right). $$

Upon some algebraic manipulation we can then obtain the final result. ∎

We can now provide the full statement of the gradient dominance of the LQR tracking problem.

#### Proposition 6 (Gradient dominance of LQR tracking).

Define

$$ \Psi^{\mathrm{opt}}=\max\left\{\lVert\Sigma^{\mathrm{opt}}\rVert_{2}+\lVert\rho^{\mathrm{opt}}\rVert_{2},\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}+\lVert\rho^{\mathrm{opt}}\rVert_{2}\right\}, $$

and

$$ \Sigma^{\mathrm{opt}}:=\mathbb{E}\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}(x_{t})^{\mathrm{opt}}((x_{t})^{\mathrm{opt}})^{\top},\quad\rho^{\mathrm{opt}}:=\mathbb{E}\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}(x_{t})^{\mathrm{opt}} $$

are the discounted state covariance matrix and mean vector respectively corresponding to an optimal policy for $J$ , and $\{x_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}}\}$ denotes the trajectory followed by the optimal policy. Suppose

$$ \mathbb{E}[x_{0}]=0,\quad\mathbb{E}[x_{0}x_{0}^{\top}]=\Sigma\succeq\alpha I\mbox{ for some }\alpha>0,\quad\lvert\rho(A+BK)\rvert<1. $$

There are two cases to consider. The first is when $x^{*}=0$ . In this case,

$$ \displaystyle J(K,\tilde{K})-J^{\mathrm{opt}}\leq\frac{\Psi^{\mathrm{opt}}}{4\alpha^{2}\sigma_{\min}(R)}\left\lVert\nabla J(K,\tilde{K})\right\rVert_{F}^{2}. $$

The second is when $x^{*}\neq 0$ . Then,

$$ \displaystyle J(K,\tilde{K})-J^{\mathrm{opt}}\leq\frac{\Psi^{\mathrm{opt}}}{4\min\{\alpha^{2},\left\lVert x^{*}\right\rVert^{2}\}\sigma_{\min}(R)}\left\lVert\nabla J(K,\tilde{K})\right\rVert_{F}^{2}. $$

Moreover, we have the following lower bound

$$ \displaystyle J(K,\tilde{K})-J^{\mathrm{opt}}\geq\frac{\min\{\alpha,1\}}{\lVert R+B^{\top}P_{K}B\rVert_{2}}\left(\lVert C_{K}\rVert_{F}^{2}+\lVert d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\rVert_{F}^{2}\right). $$

#### Proof.

Our earlier proofs of Lemmas 4, 5 and 6 filled in the gaps in our earlier proof sketch of Proposition 1. It remains for us to prove the lower bound. Consider picking

$$ K^{\prime}=K-(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)^{-1}C_{K},\quad\tilde{K}^{\prime}=\tilde{K}-(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)^{-1}d_{K,\tilde{K}}. $$

For notational simplicity, we introduce the following definitions:

$$ \displaystyle E_{K,\tilde{K}}=\begin{bmatrix}C_{K}&d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\end{bmatrix},\quad N_{K,\tilde{K}}=\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\begin{bmatrix}\mathbb{E}[(x_{t}^{\prime})(x_{t}^{\prime})^{\top}]&\mathbb{E}[x_{t}^{\prime}]\\
\mathbb{E}[(x_{t}^{\prime})^{\top}]&1\end{bmatrix}. $$

Then, since $J(K,\tilde{K})\geq J^{\mathrm{opt}}$ , it follows by the equality in (12) and our choice of $K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}$ that

$$ \displaystyle J(K,\tilde{K})-J^{\mathrm{opt}} \displaystyle\geq J(K,\tilde{K})-J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}) \displaystyle=-\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}A_{K,g}(x_{t}^{\prime},K^{\prime}x_{t}^{\prime}+\tilde{K}^{\prime}x^{*})\right] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}(C_{K}x_{t}^{\prime}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)^{-1}(C_{K}x_{t}^{\prime}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})\right] \displaystyle=\tr\left(E_{K,\tilde{K}}^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)^{-1}E_{K,\tilde{K}}N_{K,\tilde{K}})\right) \displaystyle\geq\frac{\min\{\alpha,1\}}{\lVert R+B^{\top}P_{K}B\rVert_{2}}\tr(E_{K,\tilde{K}}^{\top}E_{K,\tilde{K}}) \displaystyle=\frac{\min\{\alpha,1\}}{\lVert R+B^{\top}P_{K}B\rVert_{2}}\left(\lVert C_{K}\rVert_{F}^{2}+\lVert d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\rVert_{F}^{2}\right). $$

In obtaining the final inequality, we used the fact that

$$ \displaystyle N_{K,\tilde{K}}\succeq\begin{bmatrix}\mathbb{E}[x_{0}x_{0}^{\top}]&0\\
0&1\end{bmatrix}\succeq\min\{\alpha,1\}I, $$

where the first inequality follows from the same argument we had used for the $M_{K,\tilde{K}}$ term in the proof sketch of Proposition 1, and the second comes from our assumption that $\mathbb{E}[x_{0}x_{0}^{\top}]\succeq\min\{\alpha,1\}I.$ ∎

### B.3 Local smoothness

#### B.3.1 Outline

Suppose $(K,\tilde{K})$ is in a sublevel set $\mathcal{G}_{C}$ of $J$ for some $C>0$ , and let $(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})$ denote another policy. We start with the following observation on the cost difference between $(K,\tilde{K})$ and $(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})$ for a single agent LQR tracking problem, using our computations from Lemma 6. Recall that, defining $g^{\prime}=\tilde{K}^{\prime}x^{*}$ , and $g=\tilde{K}x^{*}$ , the advantage function

$$ A_{K,g}(x,u)=c(x,u)+\gamma V_{K,g}(Ax+Bu)-V_{K,g}(x) $$

satisfies

$$ \displaystyle A_{K,g}(x,K^{\prime}x+g^{\prime}) \displaystyle=2\tr((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(C_{K}x+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})x^{\top})+2\tr((g^{\prime}-g)^{\top}(C_{K}x+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})) \displaystyle\quad+2\tr((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(g^{\prime}-g)x^{\top}) \displaystyle\quad+\tr(xx^{\top}(K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(K^{\prime}-K))+(g^{\prime}-g)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(g^{\prime}-g) $$

As a result, applying the same analysis from Lemma 6 and taking expectations,

$$ \displaystyle J(K^{\prime},g^{\prime})-J(K,g) \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}A_{K,g}(x_{t},K^{\prime}x_{t}+g^{\prime})\right] \displaystyle=2\tr\left((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}\left(C_{K}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}x_{t}^{\prime}x_{t}^{\prime}\right]+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}(x_{t}^{\prime})^{\top}\right]\right)\right) \displaystyle\quad+2\tr\left((g^{\prime}-g)^{\top}\left(C_{K}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}x_{t}^{\prime}\right]+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\right)\right) \displaystyle\quad+2\tr\left((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(g^{\prime}-g)\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}(x_{t}^{\prime})^{\top}\right]\right) \displaystyle\quad+\tr\left(\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}x_{t}^{\prime}x_{t}^{\prime}\right](K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(K^{\prime}-K)\right)+(g^{\prime}-g)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(g^{\prime}-g) \displaystyle=2\tr((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(C_{K}\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}^{\top})) \displaystyle\quad+2\tr((g^{\prime}-g)^{\top}(C_{K}\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})) \displaystyle\quad+2\tr((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(g^{\prime}-g)\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}^{\top}) \displaystyle\quad+\tr(\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}(K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(K^{\prime}-K))+(g^{\prime}-g)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(g^{\prime}-g). $$

We note that $\{x_{t}^{\prime}\}$ refers to the trajectory obtained by the following the policy $u=K^{\prime}x+\tilde{K}^{\prime}x^{*}$ . To obtain the last equality, we recall the following definitions:

$$ \displaystyle\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}:=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}x_{t}^{\prime}x_{t}^{\prime}\right],\quad\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}:=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}x_{t}^{\prime}\right]. $$

For notational convenience, we also define

$$ \displaystyle\Psi_{(\!K,\tilde{K}\!),(\!K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}\!)}:=\left\lVert R\!+\!\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B\right\rVert_{2}\!\left(\max\!\left\{\!\left\lVert\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}\right\rVert\!,\!\left\lVert\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}\right\rVert\!,\!\left\lVert x^{*}\right\rVert^{2}\!\right\}\right). $$

Continuing from (14), and recalling that $g^{\prime}=\tilde{K}^{\prime}x^{*},g=\tilde{K}x^{*}$ , we have that

$$ \displaystyle J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})-J(K,\tilde{K})=J(K^{\prime},g^{\prime})-J(K,g) \displaystyle=2\tr((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(C_{K}\underline{\bm{\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}}}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\underline{\bm{\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}}}^{\top})) \displaystyle\ \ +2\tr((\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K})^{\top}(C_{K}\underline{\bm{\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}}}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})(x^{*})^{\top}) \displaystyle\ \ +O\left(\Psi_{(K,\tilde{K}),(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})}\left(\left\lVert K^{\prime}-K\right\rVert^{2}+\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert^{2}\right)\right) \displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(ii)}}}{{\mathstrut{\approx}}}2\tr((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(C_{K}\underline{\bm{\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}}}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\underline{\bm{\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}}}^{\top})) \displaystyle\ \ +2\tr((\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K})^{\top}(C_{K}\underline{\bm{\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}}}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})(x^{*})^{\top}) \displaystyle\ \ +O\left(\Psi_{(K,\tilde{K}),(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})}\left(\left\lVert K^{\prime}-K\right\rVert^{2}+\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert^{2}\right)\right) \displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(iii)}}}{{\mathstrut{=}}}\tr((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}\nabla_{K}J(K,\tilde{K}) \displaystyle\ \ +\tr((\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K})^{\top}\nabla_{\tilde{K}}J(K,\tilde{K}) \displaystyle\ \ +O\left(\Psi_{(K,\tilde{K}),(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})}\left(\left\lVert K^{\prime}-K\right\rVert^{2}+\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert^{2}\right)\right) \displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(iv)}}}{{\mathstrut{=}}}\tr((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}\nabla_{K}J(K,\tilde{K}) \displaystyle\ \ +\tr((\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K})^{\top}\nabla_{\tilde{K}}J(K,\tilde{K}) \displaystyle\ \ +O\left(\Psi_{C}\left(\left\lVert K^{\prime}-K\right\rVert^{2}+\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert^{2}\right)\right) $$

Above, we bolded and underlined the terms that are different before and after the approximation in (B.3.1). By constraining $\left\lVert K^{\prime}-K\right\rVert$ and $\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert$ to both be sufficiently small, it is possible to prove perturbation bounds of the form

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}-\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}\right\rVert\leq c\left(\left\lVert K^{\prime}-K\right\rVert+\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert\right), \displaystyle\left\lVert\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}-\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}\right\rVert\leq c^{\prime}\left(\left\lVert K^{\prime}-K\right\rVert+\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert\right) $$

for some positive constants $c,c^{\prime}$ depending only on $(A,B,Q,R,\Sigma,\gamma,x^{*},C)$ . This shows that the approximation in (B.3.1) is locally valid. Meanwhile, the equality in (B.3.1) holds by the form of the gradient of $J$ we computed in Lemma 5. Finally, for the equality in (B.3.1), we replaced the constant $\Psi_{(K,\tilde{K}),(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})}$ with a constant $\Psi_{C}$ , which can be shown to depend only on the sublevel set parameter $C$ as well as the system parameters $(A,B,Q,R,\Sigma,\gamma,x^{*})$ . To see why, recall that

$$ \displaystyle\Psi_{(\!K,\tilde{K}\!),(\!K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}\!)}:=\left\lVert R\!+\!\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B\right\rVert_{2}\!\left(\max\!\left\{\!\left\lVert\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}\right\rVert\!,\!\left\lVert\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}\right\rVert\!,\!\left\lVert x^{*}\right\rVert^{2}\!\right\}\right). $$

Since $(K,\tilde{K})$ lies within the sublevel set $\mathcal{G}_{C}$ , it is possible to uniformly bound the norm of $P_{K}$ , $\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}$ , as well as $\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}$ , over the set $\mathcal{G}_{C}$ . Coupled with perturbation bounds such as the ones in (15) and (16), it is not hard to see that $\Psi_{(K,\tilde{K}),(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})}$ can be replaced with a constant $\Psi_{C}$ , which depends only on the sublevel set parameter $C$ as well as the system parameters $(A,B,Q,R,\Sigma,\gamma,x^{*})$ . From (B.3.1), we see that for any $(K,\tilde{K})$ in $\mathcal{G}_{C}$ , the cost difference between it and a sufficiently close policy $(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})$ can be written as an inner product with the gradient plus some quadratic terms. By deriving norm bounds on $\nabla J(K,\tilde{K})$ uniform over any $(K,\tilde{K})$ over $\mathcal{G}_{C}$ , it follows that $J$ is locally Lipschitz within a radius $\rho$ and Lipschitz parameter $\lambda$ that hold uniformly over $\mathcal{G}_{C}$ . A similar approach allows us to prove the local Lipschitzness of the gradient of $J$ . Our argument will thus comprise the following steps:

- 1. Prove a variety of auxiliary norm bounds on terms such as

$$ P_{K},C_{K},\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}},d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*},\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}, $$

within $\mathcal{G}_{C}$ .

- 2. Prove a series of perturbation bounds of the type “assuming $(K,\tilde{K})$ is in the sublevel set $\mathcal{G}_{C}$ , if $\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert$ and $\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\rVert$ is small enough, then the difference (Term $(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})$ - Term $(K,\tilde{K})$ ) also has small norm” for various terms Term( $K,\tilde{K}$ ) depending on $K$ and $\tilde{K}$ .

- 3. Prove the local Lipschitz gradient condition within radius $\rho$ , using the preceding norm bounds and perturbation bounds.

- 4. Prove local Lipschitzness of $J$ (both population cost and sample cost) using the preceding norm bounds and perturbation bounds.

In the sequel, without loss of generality, we assume that the covariance of the initial noise distribution, $\Sigma$ , is the identity matrix $I_{n\times n}$ . We also interchangably refer to $J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})$ as $J(K^{\prime},g^{\prime})$ and $J(K,\tilde{K})$ as $J(K,g)$ , using the notation $g^{\prime}=\tilde{K}^{\prime}x^{*}$ and $g=\tilde{K}x^{*}$ .

#### Constants used in local Lipschitz and smoothness arguments.

Below is a list of constants that we will use in the local smoothness argument, where $C>0$ is the value defining the sublevel set $\mathcal{G}_{C}$ .

- • $c_{1}=\frac{\sqrt{(C-C(K^{\mathrm{opt}}))(\rho(R)+\lVert B\rVert^{2}C)}}{\sigma_{\min}(R)}+\frac{\lVert B\rVert C\lVert A\rVert}{\sigma_{\min}(R)}$

- • $c_{2}=\sqrt{\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(R)}}$

- • $c_{2}^{\prime}=c_{2}+\lVert x^{*}\rVert$

- • $c_{3}=\frac{2C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}$

- • $c_{4}=\frac{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}{4C\lVert\sqrt{\gamma}B\rVert_{2}(\lVert\sqrt{\gamma}A\rVert_{2}+\left\lVert\sqrt{\gamma}B\right\rVert_{2}c_{1}+1)}$

- • $c_{5}=\frac{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}{4\gamma\lVert B\rVert C}$ .

- • $c_{6}=\frac{1}{\sigma_{\min}(R)}\left(\sqrt{(\lVert R\rVert_{2}+\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}C)(C-J^{\mathrm{opt}})}+\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert A\rVert_{2}C\right)$

- • $c_{7}=\min\left\{\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\sqrt{(\lVert R\rVert_{2}+\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}C)(C-J^{\mathrm{opt}})},c_{6}\right\}$

- • $c_{8}=4\left(\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\right)^{2}\lVert Q\rVert_{2}\lVert B\rVert_{2}(\lVert A\rVert_{2}+\lVert B\rVert_{2}c_{7}+1)$

- • $c_{9}=8\left(\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\right)^{2}(c_{7}^{2})\lVert R\rVert_{2}\lVert B\rVert_{2}(\lVert A\rVert_{2}+\lVert B\rVert_{2}c_{7}+1)$

- • $c_{10}=2\left(\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\right)^{2}(c_{7}+1)\lVert R\rVert_{2}$

- • $c_{11}=c_{8}+c_{9}+c_{10}$

- • $c_{12}=2\gamma c_{2}^{\prime}c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2}(c_{1}+1)\lVert R\rVert_{2}+c_{2}^{\prime}\lVert R\rVert_{2}$

- • $c_{13}=2\gamma^{3/2}c_{2}^{\prime}(C+c_{11})\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}\!+\!c_{2}^{\prime}c_{3}(\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}(C+c_{11})\lVert B\rVert_{2}+\sqrt{\gamma}\lVert B\rVert_{2}c_{2}^{\prime}c_{11})$

- • $c_{14}=2\gamma c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert Qx^{*}\rVert+c_{12}+c_{13}$

- • $c_{15}=2c_{1}c_{3}\lVert R\rVert_{2}+\gamma c_{3}C\lVert B\rVert_{2}$ .

- • $c_{16}=\lVert R\rVert_{2}+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}[c_{11}+\lVert B\rVert_{2}C)]$

- • $c_{17}=\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}c_{2}^{\prime}c_{11}+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}c_{14}$

- • $c_{18}=\lVert R\rVert_{2}+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}C+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}c_{15}$

#### B.3.2 Auxiliary bounds

We first bound the terms $K$ and $g:=\tilde{K}x^{*}$ . It is helpful to build on existing results for the LQR cost with zero target in [5]. We define $f(K)$ to be the following cost, a standard LQR with tracking target $x^{*}=0$ :

$$ \begin{array}[]{ll}&f(K)=\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}x_{t}^{\top}Qx_{t}+u_{t}^{\top}Ru_{t},\\
\mbox{such that}&x_{t+1}=\sqrt{\gamma}Ax_{t}+\sqrt{\gamma}Bu_{t},\\
&u_{t}=Kx_{t},\quad x_{0}\sim N(0,\Sigma).\end{array} $$

We now show that if $J(K,\tilde{K})$ is bounded, then so is the cost $f(K)$ .

#### Lemma 7.

Consider any constant $C>0$ . Suppose $J(K,\tilde{K})\leq C$ . Then, $f(K)\leq C$ holds.

#### Proof.

Recall the notation $g:=\tilde{K}x^{*}$ . Based on Lemma 4, we see that

$$ \displaystyle J(K,g) \displaystyle=\tr(\Sigma P_{K})+\mathbb{E}[x_{0}]^{\top}q_{K,g}+r_{K,g}, \displaystyle=\tr(\Sigma P_{K})+r_{K,g}=f(K)+r_{K,g}, $$

where we used $\mathbb{E}[x_{0}]=0$ as well as the easy-to-check fact that $f(K)=\tr(\Sigma P_{K})$ . Since $r_{K,g}\geq 0$ has to hold — otherwise the value function $V(K,g;0)$ , i.e. value function of $(K,g)$ when $x_{0}=0$ , is negative —, it follows that

$$ J(K,\tilde{K})=J(K,g)=f(K)+r_{K,g}\leq C\implies f(K)\leq C. $$

∎

Consider the zero-target trajectory $\{y_{t}\}$ given by the dynamics $y_{0}=x_{0},y_{t+1}=\sqrt{\gamma}Ay_{t}+\sqrt{\gamma}BKy_{t}$ . Define

$$ \Phi_{K}:=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}y_{t}y_{t}^{\top}\right]. $$

With these definitions out of the way, we can turn to our first bounds on $\lVert K\rVert$ and $\lVert\tilde{K}x^{*}\rVert.$

#### Lemma 8 (Bound on $\lVert K\rVert,\lVert\tilde{K}x^{*}\rVert$ ).

Suppose $(K,\tilde{K})\in\mathcal{G}_{C}$ . Then, there exists constants $c_{1},c_{2}>0$ depending only on $(A,B,Q,R,\Sigma,\gamma,C)$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\lVert K\rVert\leq c_{1},\lVert\tilde{K}x^{*}\rVert\leq c_{2}. $$

#### Proof.

Since $J(K,\tilde{K})\leq C$ , $f(K)\leq C$ holds as well by Lemma 7. Thus, by Lemma 25 in [5], there exists $c_{1}$ depending only on $(A,B,Q,R,\Sigma,\gamma,C)$ such that $\lVert K\rVert\leq c_{1}$ .

We next show that $g=\tilde{K}x^{*}$ is bounded. To this end, note that the cost at $t=0$ is bounded by $C$ , namely

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[(x_{0}-x^{*})^{\top}Q(x_{0}-x^{*})+(Kx_{0}+g)^{\top}R(Kx_{0}+g)]\leq C \displaystyle\implies\tr(Q)+(x^{*})^{\top}Qx^{*}+x_{0}^{\top}(K^{\top}RK)x_{0}+g^{\top}Rg\leq C \displaystyle\implies g^{\top}Rg\leq C \displaystyle\implies\lVert g\rVert\leq\sqrt{C/\sigma_{\min}(R)}:=c_{2}. $$

∎

We next bound $\tr(\Phi_{K})$ and $\lVert P_{K}\rVert_{2}.$ This result follows directly from Lemma 13 in [5].

#### Lemma 9 (Bound on $\tr(\Phi_{K})$ and $\lVert P_{K}\rVert_{2}$ ).

Suppose $(K,\tilde{K})\in\mathcal{G}_{C}$ . Then,

$$ \displaystyle\lVert P_{K}\rVert_{2}\leq C,\quad\tr(\Phi_{K})\leq\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}. $$

We next turn to bounding the following terms:

$$ C_{K},\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}},d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*},\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}. $$

Recall that

$$ \displaystyle C_{K}=RK+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}(BK+A),\quad d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}=(R\tilde{K}+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B\tilde{K}+\gamma B^{\top}q_{K,\tilde{K}})x^{*}. $$

#### Lemma 10 (Bound on $C_{K}$ and $d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}$ ).

Suppose

$$ (K,\tilde{K})\in\mathcal{G}_{C}=\{(K,\tilde{K})\mid J(K,\tilde{K})\leq C\}. $$

Then,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert C_{K}\right\rVert_{F}^{2}\leq C\lVert R+B^{\top}P_{K}B\rVert_{2},\quad\lVert d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\rVert_{F}^{2}\leq C\lVert R+B^{\top}P_{K}B\rVert_{2}. $$

#### Proof.

From the lower bound in Proposition 6, we see that

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert C_{K}\right\rVert_{F}^{2}+\lVert d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\rVert_{F}^{2}\leq(J(K,\tilde{K})-J(K^{\mathrm{opt}},\tilde{K}^{\mathrm{opt}}))\lVert R+B^{\top}P_{K}B\rVert_{2}\leq J(K,\tilde{K})\lVert R+B^{\top}P_{K}B\rVert_{2}. $$

Using the definition of the sublevel set $\mathcal{G}_{C}$ then yields the result. ∎

We next seek to bound $\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}$ and $\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}$ . We begin with $\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}$ . Observe that

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}x_{t}\right], $$

where $\{x_{t}\}$ is generated by the policy $(K,\tilde{K})$ . Using the fact that $\mathbb{E}[x_{0}]=0$ , since $x_{t}=(A+BK)^{t}x_{0}+\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}(A+BK)^{i}B\tilde{K}x^{*}$ , we see that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[x_{t}]=\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}(A+BK)^{i}B\tilde{K}x^{*}. $$

With some algebraic manipulation, introducing the definition

$$ S_{K}:=(I-\gamma(A+BK))^{-1}, $$

we see that

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{K,\tilde{K}} \displaystyle=\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}(A+BK)^{i}B\tilde{K}x^{*}\right) \displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(v)}}}{{\mathstrut{=}}}\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}(A+BK)^{i}\right)B\tilde{K}x^{*} \displaystyle=\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}S_{K}B\tilde{K}x^{*}. $$

Above, (18) follows from rearranging the terms in the summation. Thus bounding $\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}$ reduces to bounding $S_{K}$ and $B\tilde{K}x^{*}$ . We already have a bound on the latter term from Lemma 8. This next result bounds $S_{K}$ .

#### Lemma 11 (Bound on $S_{K}$ ).

Suppose $(K,\tilde{K})\in\mathcal{G}_{C}$ . Let

$$ S_{K}:=(I-\gamma(A+BK))^{-1}. $$

Then,

$$ \displaystyle\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}\leq\frac{2C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}:=c_{3}. $$

#### Proof.

Observe now that

$$ \displaystyle\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2} \displaystyle=\rho\left((I-\gamma(A+BK))^{-1}\right) \displaystyle=\rho\left(\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}(A+BK)^{t}\right) \displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(vi)}}}{{\mathstrut{\leq}}}2\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{2t}\rho\left((A+BK)^{2t}\right) \displaystyle\leq 2\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\rho\left((A+BK)^{2t}\right) \displaystyle\leq 2\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\tr\left((\sqrt{\gamma}(A+BK))^{t}((\sqrt{\gamma}(A+BK))^{t})^{\top}\right) \displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(vii)}}}{{\mathstrut{=}}}2\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\tr\left((\sqrt{\gamma}(A+BK))^{t}\Sigma((\sqrt{\gamma}(A+BK))^{t})^{\top}\right) \displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(viii)}}}{{\mathstrut{\leq}}}2\tr(\Phi_{K})\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(ix)}}}{{\mathstrut{\leq}}}2\frac{f(K)}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(x)}}}{{\mathstrut{\leq}}}2\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}, $$

Above, inequality (B.3.2) uses the fact that $\sqrt{\gamma}\rho(A+BK)<1$ so that the even terms in the sum are larger than the odd terms, (B.3.2) uses our simplifying assumption made in the outline that $\Sigma:=\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}x_{0}x_{0}^{\top}=I$ , (B.3.2) follows from the definition of $\Phi_{K}:=\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}y_{t}y_{t}^{\top}$ , where $\{y_{t}\}$ is the zero-target trajectory given by the dynamics $y_{0}=x_{0},y_{t+1}=\sqrt{\gamma}Ay_{t}+\sqrt{\gamma}BKy_{t}$ , such that $y_{t}=(\sqrt{\gamma}(A+BK))^{t}x_{0}$ . Meanwhile, inequality (B.3.2) comes from Lemma 9, and inequality (B.3.2) follows from Lemma 7. ∎

We are now ready to bound $\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}$ .

#### Lemma 12 (Bound on $\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}$ ).

Suppose $(K,\tilde{K})\in\mathcal{G}_{C}$ . Then, recalling the definition

$$ \beta_{\gamma}=\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}, $$

we have

$$ \displaystyle\lVert\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\rVert\leq 2\beta_{\gamma}\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\lVert B\rVert c_{2}. $$

#### Proof.

From Equation 18, we have the following bound

$$ \displaystyle\lVert\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\rVert \displaystyle=\left\lVert\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}S_{K}B\tilde{K}x^{*}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\lVert S_{K}B\tilde{K}x^{*}\rVert \displaystyle\leq\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}\lVert B\rVert\lVert\tilde{K}x^{*}\rVert \displaystyle\leq\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}2\frac{f(K)}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\lVert B\rVert c_{2}\leq 2\beta_{\gamma}\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\lVert B\rVert c_{2} $$

The penultimate inequality comes from the bounds on $\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}$ and $\lVert\tilde{K}x^{*}\rVert$ from Lemma 11 and Lemma 8 respectively, while the final inequality comes from our definition of $\beta_{\gamma}$ and $f(K)\leq C$ which holds by Lemma 7. ∎

We can now turn to bounding $\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}$ . Consider defining the following linear operator on symmetric matrices, $T_{K}(\cdot)$ , as follows

$$ \displaystyle T_{K}(X):=\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}(A+BK)^{t}X[(A+BK)^{\top}]^{t}, $$

and define the induced norm of $T$ as follows:

$$ \displaystyle\lVert T_{K}\rVert=\sup_{X}\frac{\lVert T_{K}(X)\rVert}{\lVert X\rVert}. $$

We may bound the norm of $T_{K}$ as follows. We omit the proof since it follows directly from Lemma 17 in [5] applied to the system matrices $(\sqrt{\gamma}A,\sqrt{\gamma}B)$ , as well as our bound on $f(K)$ from Lemma 7.

#### Lemma 13 (Bound on $T_{K}$ norm).

We have

$$ \displaystyle\lVert T_{K}\rVert\leq\frac{f(K)}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\leq\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}. $$

#### Lemma 14 (Bound on $\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}$ ).

Suppose $(K,\tilde{K})\in\mathcal{G}_{C}$ . Then,

$$ \displaystyle\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}x_{t}x_{t}^{\top}\right]=\Phi_{K}+\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}T_{K}\left(Bg(Bg)^{\top}S_{K}^{\top}\right). $$

Moreover,

$$ \displaystyle\lVert\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}\rVert\leq\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}+\beta_{\gamma}\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\lVert B\rVert^{2}c_{2}^{2}. $$

#### Proof.

Again, recall that $g=\tilde{K}x^{*}$ . Observe that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[x_{t}x_{t}^{\top}]=\mathbb{E}[(x_{t}-\mathbb{E}[x_{t}])(x_{t}-\mathbb{E}[x_{t}])^{\top}]+\mathbb{E}[x_{t}]\mathbb{E}[x_{t}]^{\top}. $$

We first find that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}(x_{t}-\mathbb{E}[x_{t}])(x_{t}-\mathbb{E}[x_{t}])^{\top}\right] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}y_{t}y_{t}^{\top}\right]=\Phi_{K}, $$

where the sequence $\{y_{t}\}$ is the zero-target trajectory obtained by the dynamics $y_{t+1}=\sqrt{\gamma}Ay_{t}+\sqrt{\gamma}BKy_{t}$ , and we used the fact that each summand in the terms involving $g$ cancel out. Next, we have

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\mathbb{E}[x_{t}]\mathbb{E}[x_{t}^{\top}] \displaystyle=\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}(A+BK)^{i}Bg\right)\left(\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}(A+BK)^{i}Bg\right)^{\top} \displaystyle=\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}Bg(Bg)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}(A+BK)^{i}\right)^{\top} \displaystyle\quad+\gamma(A+BK)\left(\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}Bg(Bg)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}(A+BK)^{i}\right)^{\top}\right)(A+BK)^{\top} \displaystyle\quad+\gamma^{2}(A+BK)^{2}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}Bg(Bg)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}(A+BK)^{i}\right)^{\top}\right)((A+BK)^{2})^{\top} \displaystyle\quad+\cdots \displaystyle=T_{K}\left(Bg(Bg)^{\top}\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}(A+BK)^{i}\right)^{\top}\right) \displaystyle=T_{K}\left(Bg(Bg)^{\top}\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}S_{K}^{\top}\right) $$

Thus, combining, we find

$$ \displaystyle\lVert\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}\rVert \displaystyle\leq\lVert\Phi_{K}\rVert+\left\lVert T_{K}\left(Bg(Bg)^{\top}\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}S_{K}^{\top}\right)\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\lVert\Phi_{K}\rVert+\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\left\lVert T_{K}\left(Bg(Bg)^{\top}S_{K}^{\top}\right)\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\lVert\Phi_{K}\rVert+\beta_{\gamma}\lVert T_{K}\rVert\lVert Bg\rVert^{2}\left\lVert S_{K}^{\top}\right\rVert_{2}^{2} \displaystyle\leq\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}+\beta_{\gamma}\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\lVert B\rVert^{2}c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{2}. $$

For the final inequality, we used Lemma 8, Lemma 9, Lemma 11 and Lemma 13 to bound the norms of $g$ , $\Phi_{K}$ , $S_{K}$ , and $T_{K}$ respectively. ∎

#### B.3.3 Helpful perturbation bounds

We now proceed to state and prove various perturbation bounds of the type “assuming $(K,\tilde{K})$ is in the sublevel set $\mathcal{G}_{C}$ , if $\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert$ and $\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\rVert$ is small enough, then Term( $(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})$ - Term $(K,\tilde{K})$ also has small norm.” for various terms Term( $K,\tilde{K}$ ) depending on $K$ and $\tilde{K}$ .

Throughout, we first need to establish that the $K^{\prime}$ we pick has finite cost. To this end, consider the following lemma.

#### Lemma 15 (Local radius for stable $K^{\prime}$ ).

Suppose

$$ \displaystyle\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\leq\frac{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}{4C\lVert\sqrt{\gamma}B\rVert_{2}(\lVert\sqrt{\gamma}A\rVert_{2}+\left\lVert\sqrt{\gamma}B\right\rVert_{2}c_{1}+1)}:=c_{4}. $$

Then, $\sqrt{\gamma}(A+BK^{\prime})<1$ .

#### Proof.

This follows from the same argument in Lemma 22 of [5], with the system $(A,B)$ replaced by $(\sqrt{\gamma}A,\sqrt{\gamma}B)$ . ∎

Next, we seek to bound $(S_{K^{\prime}}-S_{K})$ — to be precise, we show when $K-K^{\prime}$ is small enough, $\lVert S_{K}^{\prime}-S_{K}\rVert$ can be bounded in terms of $\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert$ .

#### Lemma 16.

Suppose $(K,\tilde{K})$ is in $\mathcal{G}_{C}$ . Suppose $\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\leq c_{4}$ , so $\sqrt{\gamma}\rho(A+BK^{\prime})<1$ , and that $\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\leq\frac{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}{4\gamma\lVert B\rVert C}:=c_{5}$ . Then,

$$ \displaystyle\lVert S_{K^{\prime}}-S_{K}\rVert\leq 2\gamma c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert,\quad\mbox{and}\quad\lVert S_{K^{\prime}}\rVert_{2}\leq 2\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}. $$

#### Proof.

For notational convenience, in this proof, we define

$$ D:=I-\gamma(A+BK),\quad E:=\gamma B(K-K^{\prime}). $$

Then, we have

$$ \displaystyle S_{K^{\prime}}-S_{K} \displaystyle=(D+E)^{-1}-D^{-1} \displaystyle=D^{-1}\left(I+ED^{-1}\right)^{-1}-D^{-1} \displaystyle=D^{-1}\left((I+ED^{-1})^{-1}-I\right) $$

Next, consider $I+ED^{-1}$ . Observe that

$$ \displaystyle(I+ED^{-1})^{-1}=I-(I+ED^{-1})^{-1}ED^{-1}, $$

which can be verified by multiplying both sides with $I+ED^{-1}$ . Note now that

$$ \displaystyle\lVert ED^{-1}\rVert \displaystyle=\left\lVert\gamma B(K-K^{\prime})S_{K}\right\rVert\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(xi)}}}{{\mathstrut{\leq}}}\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}(\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(xii)}}}{{\mathstrut{\leq}}}\frac{1}{2}, $$

where the inequality in (21) holds because $\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}\leq\frac{2C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}$ from Lemma 11 and our assumption that $\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\leq\frac{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}{4\gamma\lVert B\rVert C}$ . Continuing with equation (20), we note that

$$ \displaystyle\quad(I+ED^{-1})^{-1}=I-(I+ED^{-1})^{-1}ED^{-1} \displaystyle\implies\left\lVert(I+ED^{-1})^{-1}\right\rVert_{2}\leq\left\lVert I\right\rVert_{2}+\left\lVert(I+ED^{-1})^{-1}ED^{-1}\right\rVert_{2} \displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(xiii)}}}{{\mathstrut{\implies}}}\left\lVert(I+ED^{-1})^{-1}\right\rVert_{2}\leq\left\lVert I\right\rVert_{2}+\frac{1}{2}\left\lVert(I+ED^{-1})^{-1}\right\rVert_{2} \displaystyle\implies\frac{1}{2}\left\lVert(I+ED^{-1})^{-1}\right\rVert_{2}\leq 1\implies\left\lVert(I+ED^{-1})^{-1}\right\rVert_{2}\leq 2. $$

Above, (22) follows from (21).

Therefore, combining equations (19) and (20), we have that

$$ \displaystyle S_{K^{\prime}}-S_{K} \displaystyle=D^{-1}\left((I+ED^{-1})^{-1}-I\right)=D^{-1}(-(I+ED^{-1})^{-1}ED^{-1}), $$

which implies that

$$ \displaystyle\lVert S_{K^{\prime}}-S_{K}\rVert \displaystyle=\lVert D^{-1}(-(I+ED^{-1})^{-1}ED^{-1})\rVert \displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(xiv)}}}{{\mathstrut{\leq}}}\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}\left\lVert(I+ED^{-1})^{-1}\right\rVert_{2}\left\lVert ED^{-1}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq 2\gamma c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert $$

Above, the final inequality follows from the bound on $\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}$ from Lemma 11, the bound on $\left\lVert(I+ED^{-1})^{-1}\right\rVert_{2}$ from (22), and the bound on $\left\lVert ED^{-1}\right\rVert$ in (21) of equation (21). Meanwhile, it follows from (B.3.3) and the bounds in (21) and (22) that

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert S_{K^{\prime}}-S_{K}\right\rVert_{2}\leq\left\lVert S_{K}\right\rVert_{2}. $$

∎

Next, we bound the norm of $(T_{K^{\prime}}-T_{K})$ when $K^{\prime}$ is close to $K$ . The result follows from Equation (30b) of [6], with the system matrices $(A,B)$ replaced by $(\sqrt{\gamma}A,\sqrt{\gamma}B)$ .

#### Lemma 17 (Bound on norm of $(T_{K^{\prime}}-T_{K})$ ).

Suppose $(K,\tilde{K})\in\mathcal{G}_{C}$ , and that $\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\leq c_{4}$ . Then,

$$ \displaystyle\lVert T_{K^{\prime}}-T_{K}\rVert\leq c_{5}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert, $$

where $c_{5}:=\frac{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}{4\gamma\lVert B\rVert C}$ was defined earlier.

Next, we bound the norm of $(P_{K}-P_{K^{\prime}})$ and $f(K^{\prime})-f(K)$ when $K^{\prime}$ is close to $K$ . The result follows from Lemma 13 of [5], with the system matrices $(A,B)$ replaced by $(\sqrt{\gamma}A,\sqrt{\gamma}B)$ .

#### Lemma 18 (Bound on norm of $P_{K^{\prime}}-P_{K}$ and $f(K^{\prime})-f(K)$ ).

Suppose $(K,\tilde{K})\in\mathcal{G}_{C}$ , and that $\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\leq\min\{c_{4},c_{5}\}$ . Then, there exists a constant $c_{11}>0$ depending only on $(A,B,Q,R,\Sigma,x^{*},\gamma,C)$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\lVert P_{K^{\prime}}-P_{K}\rVert_{2}\leq c_{11}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert,\quad\lvert f(K^{\prime})-f(K)\rvert\leq nc_{11}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert. $$

We turn now to bounding $\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}-\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}$ .

#### Lemma 19 (Bound on $\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}-\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}$ ).

Suppose

$$ (K,\tilde{K})\in\mathcal{G}_{C},\quad\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\leq\min\{c_{4},c_{5}\}. $$

Then,

$$ \displaystyle\lVert\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}-\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}\rVert \displaystyle\leq 4\gamma\beta_{\gamma}\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\lVert B\rVert^{2}c_{2}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+\beta_{\gamma}\frac{4C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\lVert B\rVert\lVert x^{*}\rVert\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\rVert. $$

#### Proof.

Note that

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}-\rho_{K,\tilde{K}} \displaystyle=\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}S_{K^{\prime}}B\tilde{K}^{\prime}x^{*}-\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}S_{K}B\tilde{K}x^{*} \displaystyle=\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\left(S_{K^{\prime}}B\tilde{K}x^{*}+S_{K^{\prime}}B(\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K})x^{*}\right)-\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}S_{K}B\tilde{K}x^{*} \displaystyle=\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}(S_{K^{\prime}}-S_{K})B\tilde{K}x^{*}+\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}S_{K^{\prime}}B(\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K})x^{*}. $$

Then,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}-\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}\right\rVert \displaystyle=\left\lVert\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}(S_{K^{\prime}}-S_{K})B\tilde{K}x^{*}+\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}S_{K^{\prime}}B(\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K})x^{*}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\left\lVert\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}(S_{K^{\prime}}-S_{K})B\tilde{K}x^{*}\right\rVert+\left\lVert\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}S_{K^{\prime}}B(\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K})x^{*}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\beta_{\gamma}2\gamma\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}\lVert B\rVert\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\lVert B\rVert\lVert\tilde{K}x^{*}\rVert+\beta_{\gamma}\lVert S_{K^{\prime}}\rVert\lVert B\rVert\lVert x^{*}\rVert\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\rVert \displaystyle\leq 4\gamma\beta_{\gamma}\frac{C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\lVert B\rVert^{2}c_{2}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+\beta_{\gamma}\frac{4C}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\lVert B\rVert\lVert x^{*}\rVert\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\rVert. $$

The penultimate inequality comes from the perturbation bound on $\left\lVert S_{K^{\prime}}-S_{K}\right\rVert_{2}$ in Lemma 16, our assumption that $\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\leq c_{5}$ , and the norm bound on $\tilde{K}x^{*}$ in Lemma 8. For the final inequality, we used the fact that $\lVert S_{K^{\prime}}\rVert_{2}\leq 2\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}$ , which we derived in Lemma 16. ∎

We next bound $\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}-\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}$ .

#### Lemma 20 (Bound on $\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}-\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}$ ).

Suppose

$$ (K,\tilde{K})\in\mathcal{G}_{C},\quad\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\leq\min\{c_{4},c_{5},1\},\quad\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert\leq 1. $$

Then,

$$ \displaystyle\lVert\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}-\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}\rVert \displaystyle\leq\left(c_{6}+\lVert B\rVert^{2}(c_{2}^{\prime})^{2})(2\gamma c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2})+(4c_{3}^{2})c_{5}\lVert B\rVert^{2}(c_{2}^{\prime})^{2}\right)\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+\beta_{\gamma}\left(\frac{c_{3}C\lVert x^{*}\rVert}{\sigma_{\min}(Q)}\left(\left\lVert B\right\rVert^{2}c_{2}^{\prime}+c_{2}\right)\right)\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert. $$

#### Proof.

Note that

$$ \displaystyle\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}-\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}} \displaystyle=\left(\Phi_{K^{\prime}}+\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}T_{K^{\prime}}\left((B\tilde{K}^{\prime}x^{*})(B\tilde{K}^{\prime}x^{*})^{\top}S_{K^{\prime}}^{\top}\right)\right)-\left(\Phi_{K}+\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}T_{K}\left((B\tilde{K}x^{*})(B\tilde{K}x^{*})^{\top}S_{K}^{\top}\right)\right). $$

We first bound $\Phi_{K^{\prime}}-\Phi_{K}$ . To this end, observe that by Lemma 16 in [5], there exists $c_{6}>0$ depending only on $(A,B,Q,R,\Sigma,\gamma,C)$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\Phi_{K^{\prime}}-\Phi_{K}\right\rVert\leq c_{6}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert. $$

Meanwhile, recalling that $g:=\tilde{K}x^{*}$ and $g^{\prime}:=\tilde{K}^{\prime}x^{*}$ , observe that by our assumption on $\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert\leq 1$ , it follows that

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert g^{\prime}-g\right\rVert\leq\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert\lVert x^{*}\rVert\leq\lVert x^{*}\rVert, $$

which implies that

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert g^{\prime}\right\rVert\leq\lVert g\rVert+\lVert x^{*}\rVert\leq c_{2}+\lVert x^{*}\rVert:=c_{2}^{\prime}, $$

where the bound on $\lVert g\rVert$ comes from Lemma 8. Then,

$$ g^{\prime}(g-g^{\prime})^{\top}\right\rVert+\left\lVert(g^{\prime}-g)(g)^{\top}\right\rVert\right)+(\lVert B\rVert^{2}(c_{2}^{\prime})^{2})(2\gamma c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2})\lVert #### Lemma 21.

Suppose

For notational simplicity, throughout, we denote

$$ q_{K^{\prime},g^{\prime}}:=q_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}x^{*},\quad q_{K,g}:=q_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}. $$

Next, observe that

$$ \displaystyle\lVert S_{K^{\prime}}^{\top}(K^{\prime})^{\top}Rg^{\prime}-S_{K}^{\top}K^{\top}Rg\rVert \displaystyle=\lVert(S_{K^{\prime}}^{\top}-S_{K}^{\top})((K^{\prime})^{\top}Rg^{\prime})+S_{K}^{\top}((K^{\prime})^{\top}Rg^{\prime})-S_{K}^{\top}K^{\top}Rg\rVert \displaystyle=\lVert(S_{K^{\prime}}^{\top}-S_{K}^{\top})((K^{\prime})^{\top}Rg^{\prime})+S_{K}^{\top}((K^{\prime})^{\top}Rg^{\prime}-K^{\top}Rg)+S_{K}^{\top}K^{\top}Rg-S_{K}^{\top}K^{\top}Rg\rVert \displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(xvi)}}}{{\mathstrut{\leq}}}2\gamma c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert((\lVert K\rVert+1)\lVert R\rVert_{2}\lVert g^{\prime}\rVert \displaystyle\hskip 9.24994pt+2c_{3}\left(\left\lVert K^{\top}R(g^{\prime}-g)+(K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}Rg+(K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}R(g^{\prime}-g)\right\rVert\right) \displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(xvii)}}}{{\mathstrut{\leq}}}2\gamma c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2}(c_{1}+1)c_{2}^{\prime}\lVert R\rVert_{2}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert \displaystyle\hskip 9.24994pt+2c_{3}\left(\lVert K\rVert\lVert R\rVert_{2}\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert+\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\lVert R\rVert_{2}\lVert g\rVert+\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\lVert R\rVert_{2}\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert\right) \displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(xviii)}}}{{\mathstrut{\leq}}}2\gamma c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2}(c_{1}+1)c_{2}^{\prime}\lVert R\rVert_{2}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert \displaystyle\hskip 9.24994pt+2c_{3}(c_{1}\lVert R\rVert_{2}\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert+\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\lVert R\rVert_{2}c_{2}+\lVert R\rVert_{2}\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert) \displaystyle=\left(2\gamma c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2}(c_{1}+1)c_{2}^{\prime}\lVert R\rVert_{2}+\lVert R\rVert_{2}c_{2}\right)\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+(2c_{1}c_{3}+1)\lVert R\rVert_{2}\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert \displaystyle=\left(2\gamma c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2}(c_{1}+1)c_{2}^{\prime}\lVert R\rVert_{2}+c_{2}\lVert R\rVert_{2}\right)\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+(2c_{1}c_{3}+1)\lVert R\rVert_{2}\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert $$

Above, (27) follows from the perturbation bound on $\lVert S_{K^{\prime}}-S_{K}\rVert_{2}$ in Lemma 16, the bound on $\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}$ in Lemma 11, and our assumption that $\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\leq 1$ . Meanwhile, (27) and (27) both hold due to our bounds on $K$ Lemma 8, our assumption that $\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\leq 1$ , as well as the bound on $\lVert g^{\prime}\rVert$ on Line 24.

We next turn to the last summand in (25), namely

$$ \left(\gamma S_{K^{\prime}}^{\top}(A+BK^{\prime})^{\top}P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}-\gamma S_{K}^{\top}(A+BK)^{\top}P_{K}Bg\right). $$

By a similar algebraic manipulation to the immediately preceding set of derivations, we find that

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\gamma S_{K^{\prime}}^{\top}(A+BK^{\prime})^{\top}P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}-\gamma S_{K}^{\top}(A+BK)^{\top}P_{K}Bg\right\rVert \displaystyle=\left\lVert(S_{K^{\prime}}^{\top}-S_{K}^{\top})\gamma(A+BK^{\prime})^{\top}P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}+S_{K}^{\top}(\gamma(A+BK^{\prime})^{\top}P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}-\gamma(A+BK)^{\top}P_{K}Bg)\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\gamma\lVert S_{K^{\prime}}^{\top}-S_{K}^{\top}\rVert\lVert(A+BK^{\prime})^{\top}P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}\rVert_{2}+\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}\lVert\gamma(A+BK^{\prime})^{\top}P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}-\gamma(A+BK)^{\top}P_{K}Bg\rVert. $$

We first handle $\gamma\lVert S_{K^{\prime}}-S_{K}\rVert\lVert(A+BK^{\prime})^{\top}P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}\rVert_{2}$ . This involves bounding $\sqrt{\gamma}\lVert(A+BK^{\prime})^{\top}P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}\rVert_{2}$ . To this end, observe that

$$ \displaystyle\sqrt{\gamma}\lVert(A+BK^{\prime})^{\top}P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}\rVert_{2} \displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(xix)}}}{{\mathstrut{\leq}}}\lVert P_{K^{\prime}}\rVert_{2}\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert g^{\prime}\rVert \displaystyle=\lVert P_{K}+P_{K^{\prime}}-P_{K}\rVert_{2}\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert g^{\prime}\rVert \displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(xx)}}}{{\mathstrut{\leq}}}(\lVert P_{K}\rVert_{2}+c_{11}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert)\lVert B\rVert_{2}(c_{2}^{\prime}) \displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\textnormal{(xxi)}}}{{\mathstrut{\leq}}}(C+c_{11})c_{2}^{\prime}\lVert B\rVert_{2} $$

Above, (B.3.3) holds due to our choice of $K^{\prime}$ such that $\sqrt{\rho}\lVert A+BK^{\prime}\rVert\leq 1$ , while (B.3.3) holds due to Lemma 18 which bounds $\lVert P_{K}+P_{K^{\prime}}-P_{K}\rVert_{2}$ as well as the fact that $\lVert g^{\prime}\rVert\leq c_{2}^{\prime}$ , which we have seen earlier. Finally, (B.3.3) comes from the bound on $\lVert P_{K}\rVert_{2}$ in Lemma 9. By Lemma 16 which bounds $\lVert S_{K^{\prime}}-S_{K}\rVert$ , this gives us

$$ \displaystyle\gamma\lVert S_{K^{\prime}}-S_{K}\rVert\lVert(A+BK^{\prime})^{\top}P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}\rVert \displaystyle\leq\sqrt{\gamma}(C+c_{11})c_{2}^{\prime}\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert S_{K^{\prime}}-S_{K}\rVert \displaystyle\leq\sqrt{\gamma}(C+c_{11})c_{2}^{\prime}\lVert B\rVert_{2}\left(2\gamma\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\right) \displaystyle\leq 2\gamma^{3/2}(C+c_{11})c_{2}^{\prime}\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert. $$

Next, we handle $\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}\lVert\gamma(A+BK^{\prime})^{\top}P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}-\gamma(A+BK)^{\top}P_{K}Bg\rVert$ . Following a similar application of relevant norm and perturbation bounds, we find that

$$ \displaystyle\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}\lVert\gamma(A+BK^{\prime})^{\top}P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}-\gamma(A+BK)^{\top}P_{K}Bg\rVert_{2} \displaystyle=\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}\left\lVert\gamma((A+BK^{\prime})^{\top}-(A+BK)^{\top})P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}+\gamma(A+BK)^{\top}(P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}-P_{K}Bg)\right\rVert \displaystyle=\lVert S_{K}\rVert_{2}\left\lVert\gamma((A+BK^{\prime})^{\top}-(A+BK)^{\top})\right\rVert\left\lVert P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}\right\rVert+\gamma\left\lVert(A+BK)^{\top}\left((P_{K^{\prime}}-P_{K})Bg^{\prime}+P_{K}B(g^{\prime}-g)\right)\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\gamma c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert(C+c_{11})c_{2}^{\prime}\lVert B\rVert_{2}+\sqrt{\gamma}c_{3}\left(\lVert P_{K^{\prime}}-P_{K}\rVert\lVert B\rVert_{2}c_{2}^{\prime}\right)+\gamma\lVert P_{K}\rVert_{2}\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert \displaystyle\leq\gamma c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}(C+c_{11})c_{2}^{\prime}\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+\sqrt{\gamma}c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2}c_{2}^{\prime}c_{11}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+C\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert \displaystyle\leq c_{3}(\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}(C+c_{11})c_{2}^{\prime}\lVert B\rVert_{2}+\sqrt{\gamma}\lVert B\rVert_{2}c_{2}^{\prime}c_{11})\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+\gamma c_{3}C\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert. $$

Define now

$$ \displaystyle c_{12}:=2\gamma c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2}(c_{1}+1)c_{2}^{\prime}\lVert R\rVert_{2}+c_{2}\lVert R\rVert_{2}, \displaystyle c_{13}:=2\gamma^{3/2}(C+c_{11})c_{2}^{\prime}\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}+c_{3}(\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}(C+c_{11})c_{2}^{\prime}\lVert B\rVert_{2}+\sqrt{\gamma}\lVert B\rVert_{2}c_{2}^{\prime}c_{11}). $$

Then, combining the bounds in (26), (27), (28), and (29), we find that

$$ \displaystyle\lVert q_{K^{\prime},g^{\prime}}-q_{K,g}\rVert \displaystyle\leq(2\gamma c_{3}\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert Qx^{*}\rVert+c_{12}+c_{13})\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+\left((2c_{1}c_{3}+1)\lVert R\rVert_{2}+\gamma c_{3}C\lVert B\rVert_{2}\right)\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert. $$

#### Lemma 22.

Suppose

$$ (K,\tilde{K})\in\mathcal{G}_{C},\quad\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\leq\min\{c_{4},c_{5},1\},\quad\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\rVert\leq 1. $$

Then,

$$ \displaystyle\lVert C_{K^{\prime}}-C_{K}\rVert\leq c_{16}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert \displaystyle\lVert d_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}x^{*}-d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\rVert\leq c_{17}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+c_{18}\lVert x^{*}\rVert\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\rVert, $$

where

$$ \displaystyle c_{16}=\lVert R\rVert_{2}+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}[c_{11}+\lVert B\rVert_{2}C)] \displaystyle c_{17}=\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}c_{2}^{\prime}c_{11}+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}c_{14} \displaystyle c_{18}=\lVert R\rVert_{2}+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}C+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}c_{15}. $$

#### Proof.

For notational simplicity, we denote

$$ d_{K^{\prime},g^{\prime}}:=d_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}x^{*},\quad d_{K,g}:=d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}. $$

We first handle $C_{K^{\prime}}-C_{K}$ . Using norm bounds on $K,g$ , perturbation bounds on $\lVert P_{K^{\prime}}-P_{K}\rVert$ , and our assumptions on $K^{\prime}$ , we find that

$$ \displaystyle\lVert C_{K^{\prime}}-C_{K}\rVert \displaystyle\leq\lVert RK^{\prime}+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K^{\prime}}(BK^{\prime}+A)-(RK+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}(BK+A))\rVert \displaystyle\leq\lVert R\rVert_{2}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert(P_{K^{\prime}}-P_{K})(A+BK^{\prime})+P_{K}B(K^{\prime}-K)\rVert \displaystyle\leq\lVert R\rVert_{2}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}[c_{11}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+\lVert B\rVert_{2}C\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert] \displaystyle=(\lVert R\rVert_{2}+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}[c_{11}+\lVert B\rVert_{2}C)])\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert. $$

Meanwhile, using norm bounds on $K,g$ , perturbation bounds on $\lVert P_{K^{\prime}}-P_{K}\rVert$ and $\left\lVert q_{K^{\prime},g^{\prime}}-q_{K,g}\right\rVert$ , we find that

$$ \displaystyle\lVert d_{K^{\prime},g^{\prime}}-d_{K,g}\rVert \displaystyle=\lVert Rg^{\prime}+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K^{\prime}}Bg^{\prime}+\gamma B^{\top}q_{K^{\prime},g^{\prime}}-(Rg+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}Bg+\gamma B^{\top}q_{K,g})\rVert \displaystyle\leq\lVert R\rVert_{2}\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert(P_{K^{\prime}}-P_{K})Bg^{\prime}+P_{K}B(g^{\prime}-g)\rVert+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert q_{K^{\prime},g^{\prime}}-q_{K,g}\rVert \displaystyle\leq\lVert R\rVert_{2}\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}(\lVert B\rVert_{2}c_{2}^{\prime}c_{11}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+C\lVert B\rVert_{2}\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert) \displaystyle\quad+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}(c_{14}\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+c_{15}\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert) \displaystyle\leq(\lVert R\rVert_{2}+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}C+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}c_{15})\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert+(\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}^{2}c_{2}^{\prime}c_{11}+\gamma\lVert B\rVert_{2}c_{14})\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert. $$

#### B.3.4 Local Lipschitzness of $\nabla J$

We are now finally ready to combine the various norm and perturbation bounds to show that $J$ has locally Lipschitz gradient.

#### Proposition 7 ( $\nabla J(K,\tilde{K})$ is locally Lipschitz).

Suppose

$$ (K,\tilde{K})\in\mathcal{G}_{C},\quad\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\leq\min\{c_{4},c_{5},1\},\quad\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\rVert\leq 1. $$

Then, there exists $L>0$ depending only on $(A,B,Q,R,\Sigma,\gamma,x^{*},C)$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\lVert\nabla J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})-\nabla J(K,\tilde{K})\rVert\leq L\left(\left\lVert K^{\prime}-K\right\rVert+\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert\right). $$

#### Proof.

We seek to bound $\left\lVert\nabla J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})-\nabla J(K,\tilde{K})\right\rVert^{2}$ . We consider the derivative terms in $K$ and $\tilde{K}$ separately. We first tackle $\lVert\nabla_{K}J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})-\nabla_{K}J(K,\tilde{K})\rVert$ . From Lemma 5, we know that

$$ \displaystyle\nabla_{K}J(K,\tilde{K}) \displaystyle=2C_{K}\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}+2d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}^{\top}, $$

Hence,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\nabla_{K}J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})-\nabla_{K}J(K,\tilde{K})\right\rVert \displaystyle=\left\lVert 2C_{K^{\prime}}\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}+2d_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}x^{*}\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}^{\top}-\left(2C_{K}\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}+2d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}^{\top}\right)\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq 2\left\lVert C_{K^{\prime}}\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}+C_{K^{\prime}}(\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}-\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}})-C_{K}\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}\right\rVert \displaystyle\quad+2\left\lVert d_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}x^{*}\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}^{\top}+d_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}x^{*}(\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}^{\top}-\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}^{\top})-d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}^{\top}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq 2\left\lVert(C_{K^{\prime}}-C_{K})\right\rVert\left\lVert\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}\right\rVert+2\left\lVert C_{K^{\prime}}\right\rVert\left\lVert\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}-\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}}\right\rVert \displaystyle\quad+2\left\lVert d_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}x^{*}-d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\right\rVert\left\lVert\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}\right\rVert+2\left\lVert d_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}x^{*}\right\rVert\left\lVert\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}-\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}\right\rVert $$

By the perturbation bounds in Lemma 22 as well as Lemma 20 and Lemma 19, as well as bounds on the norms of $\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}},\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*},C_{K},d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}$ we derived in Lemma 14, Lemma 12, and Lemma 10 respectively, it follows that there exists $c^{\prime\prime}>0$ depending only on $(A,B,Q,R,\Sigma,\gamma,x^{*},C)$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\nabla_{K}J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})-\nabla_{K}J(K,\tilde{K})\right\rVert\leq c^{\prime\prime}\left(\left\lVert K^{\prime}-K\right\rVert+\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert\right). $$

It remains to bound $\left\lVert\nabla_{\tilde{K}}J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})-\nabla_{\tilde{K}}J(K,\tilde{K})\right\rVert$ . To this end, recall $\nabla_{\tilde{K}}J$ which we computed in Lemma 5, giving us

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\nabla_{\tilde{K}}J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})-\nabla_{\tilde{K}}J(K,\tilde{K})\right\rVert \displaystyle=\left\lVert 2(C_{K^{\prime}}\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}x^{*}+d_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}x^{*}(x^{*})^{\top})-2(C_{K}\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}(x^{*})^{\top})\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq 2\left\lVert C_{K^{\prime}}\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}+C_{K^{\prime}}(\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}-\rho_{K,\tilde{K}})x^{*}-C_{K}\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\right\rVert \displaystyle\quad+2\left\lVert d_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}x^{*}(x^{*})^{\top}-d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}(x^{*})^{\top}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq 2\left\lVert(C_{K^{\prime}}-C_{K})\right\rVert\left\lVert\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\right\rVert+2\left\lVert C_{K^{\prime}}\right\rVert\left\lVert\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}x^{*}-\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\right\rVert \displaystyle\quad+2\left\lVert d_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}x^{*}(x^{*})^{\top}-d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}(x^{*})^{\top}\right\rVert. $$

By the perturbation bounds in Lemma 22 and Lemma 19, as well as bounds on the norms of $\rho_{K,\tilde{K}},C_{K},d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}$ we derived in Lemma 12 and Lemma 10 respectively, it follows that there exists $c^{\prime\prime\prime}>0$ depending only on $(A,B,Q,R,\Sigma,\gamma,x^{*},C)$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\nabla_{\tilde{K}}J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})-\nabla_{\tilde{K}}J(K,\tilde{K})\right\rVert\leq c^{\prime\prime\prime}\left(\left\lVert K^{\prime}-K\right\rVert+\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert\right). $$

The statement in the lemma then follows by picking a $L$ depending only on the constants $c,c^{\prime},c^{\prime\prime},c^{\prime\prime\prime}$ . ∎

#### B.3.5 Local Lipschitzness of $J$

We now state and prove the local Lipschitz property of $J(K,\tilde{K})$ .

#### Proposition 8 (Local Lipschitzness of $J(K,\tilde{K})$ ).

Suppose

$$ (K,\tilde{K})\in\mathcal{G}_{C},\quad\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\leq\min\{c_{4},c_{5},1\},\quad\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\rVert\leq 1. $$

Then, there exists $\lambda>0$ depending only on $(A,B,Q,R,\Sigma,\gamma,x^{*},C)$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\lvert J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})-J(K,\tilde{K})\rvert\leq\lambda\left(\left\lVert K^{\prime}-K\right\rVert+\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert\right). $$

#### Proof.

Recall from Line (14) in our computations in the outline that

$$ \displaystyle J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})-J(K,\tilde{K}) \displaystyle=2\tr((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(C_{K}\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*}\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}^{\top}))+2\tr((\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K})^{\top}(C_{K}\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}+d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*})(x^{*})^{\top}) \displaystyle\quad+2\tr((K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K})x^{*}\rho_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}^{\top}) \displaystyle\quad+\tr(\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}}(K^{\prime}-K)^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(K^{\prime}-K))+\tr((\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K})^{\top}(R+\gamma B^{\top}P_{K}B)(\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K})x^{*}(x^{*})^{\top}). $$

Since we have bounds on the terms

$$ \displaystyle C_{K},\Sigma_{K,\tilde{K}},d_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*},\rho_{K,\tilde{K}}x^{*},P_{K},\tilde{K}x^{*}, $$

from Lemmas (8), (9), (12),(14) , and (22), by our choice of $K^{\prime}$ and $\tilde{K}^{\prime}$ , applying the perturbation bounds in Lemmas (19) and (20), we have bounds on

$$ \displaystyle\Sigma_{K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime}},\rho_{K,\tilde{K}} $$

as well. Therefore, it follows that there exists $\lambda>0$ depending only on $(A,B,Q,R,\Sigma,\gamma,x^{*},C)$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\lvert J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime})-J(K,\tilde{K})\rvert\leq\lambda\left(\left\lVert K^{\prime}-K\right\rVert+\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert\right). $$

∎

Finally, we need to show a local Lipschitz property for the sample cost variant $J(K,\tilde{K};x_{0}))$ starting from an initial state $x_{0}$ . To facilitate technical analysis, we work with the assumption $\lVert x_{0}\rVert\leq C_{n}$ for some $C_{n}>0$ (cf. [6]).

#### Proposition 9 (Local Lipschitzness of sample cost $J(K,\tilde{K};x_{0})$ ).

Suppose

$$ (K,\tilde{K})\in\mathcal{G}_{C},\quad\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert\leq\min\{c_{4},c_{5},1\},\quad\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\rVert\leq 1,\quad\lVert x_{0}\rVert\leq C_{n}. $$

Then, there exists $\lambda>0$ depending only on $(A,B,Q,R,\Sigma,\gamma,x^{*},C,C_{n})$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\lvert J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime};x_{0})-J(K,\tilde{K};x_{0})\rvert\leq\lambda\left(\left\lVert K^{\prime}-K\right\rVert+\left\lVert\tilde{K}^{\prime}-\tilde{K}\right\rVert\right). $$

#### Proof.

We note that by Lemma 4, recalling that $g:=\tilde{K}x^{*}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle J(K,\tilde{K};x_{0})=x_{0}^{\top}P_{K}x_{0}+x_{0}^{\top}q_{K,g}+r_{K,g}. $$

Since we already have perturbation bounds on $\lVert P_{K}-P_{K^{\prime}}\rVert$ and $q_{K,g}$ from Lemma 18 and 21 respectively for $K^{\prime}$ and $\tilde{K}^{\prime}$ selected as in the assumptions, it remains for us to bound $r_{K^{\prime},g^{\prime}}-r_{K^{\prime},g^{\prime}}$ . From Lemma 4, we have that

$$ \displaystyle r_{K,g}=\frac{1}{1-\gamma}\left((x^{*})^{\top}Qx^{*}+g^{\top}Rg+\gamma\left(g^{\top}B^{\top}P_{K}Bg+2g^{\top}B^{\top}q_{K,g}\right)\right). $$

By the perturbation techniques used earlier, it is clear from the form of $r_{K,g}$ that there exists $c>0$ depending only on $(A,B,Q,R,\Sigma,\gamma,x^{*},C)$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\lvert r_{K^{\prime},g^{\prime}}-r_{K,g}\rvert\leq c(\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert). $$

Therefore, since we also assumed an uniform bound $C_{n}$ on $\lVert x_{0}\rVert$ , there exists a $\lambda>0$ depending only on $(A,B,Q,R,\Sigma,\gamma,x^{*},C,C_{n})$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\lvert J(K^{\prime},\tilde{K}^{\prime};x_{0})-J(K,\tilde{K};x_{0})\rvert\leq\lambda(\lVert K^{\prime}-K\rVert+\lVert g^{\prime}-g\rVert). $$

The following results from zeroth-order optimization are useful. The two-point estimators we use in the algorithm can be defined as follows:

$$ \displaystyle z_{r}((K,\tilde{K}),x_{0}^{i},\delta^{i}):=\frac{d}{2r}\left(J((K,\tilde{K})+r\delta^{i};x_{0}^{i})-J(((K,\tilde{K})-r\delta^{i};(x_{0})^{i})\right)\delta^{i}, $$

where $i\in[m]$ denotes the indexing in the mini-batch, and $d=2nk$ (i.e. dimension of $K$ plus dimension of $\tilde{K}$ ). When the context is clear, we may some times omit the index $i$ . An essential quantity is the following smoothed version of $J$ :

$$ \displaystyle J_{r}(K,\tilde{K})=\mathbb{E}_{\bar{\delta}\sim\mathbb{B}^{d}}\left[J(K,\tilde{K})+r\bar{\delta}\right]. $$

This next lemma shows that the zeroth-order estimator $z_{r}$ is an unbiased estimate of $\nabla J_{r}(K,\tilde{K})$ , which in turn is close to $\nabla J(K,\tilde{K})$ when $r$ is small.

- 2. The gradient of the smoothed version of $J$ is close to the gradient of $J$ .

$$ \lVert\nabla J_{r}(K,\tilde{K})-\nabla J(K,\tilde{K})\rVert\leq rL. $$

- 3. There exists a maximum bound on the size of each estimate: $\displaystyle\sup_{\begin{subarray}{c}\hat{K}\in\mathcal{G}_{10J_{0}}\\ x_{0},\delta\end{subarray}}\left\{\left\lVert z_{r}(\hat{K};x_{0},\delta)\right\rVert\right\}\leq d\lambda,$ where $\lambda$ is the local Lipschitz parameter defined earlier.

Therefore, for the two-point estimator, we can set

Federated learning (FL) is a method used for training artificial intelligence models with data from multiple sources while maintaining data anonymity, thus removing many barriers to data sharing. Here we used data from 20 institutes across the globe to train a FL model, called EXAM (electronic medical record (EMR) chest X-ray AI model), that predicts the future oxygen requirements of symptomatic patients with COVID-19 using inputs of vital signs, laboratory data and chest X-rays. EXAM achieved an average area under the curve (AUC) >0.92 for predicting outcomes at 24 and 72 h from the time of initial presentation to the emergency room, and it provided 16% improvement in average AUC measured across all participating sites and an average increase in generalizability of 38% when compared with models trained at a single site using that site’s data. For prediction of mechanical ventilation treatment or death at 24 h at the largest independent test site, EXAM achieved a sensitivity of 0.950 and specificity of 0.882. In this study, FL facilitated rapid data science collaboration without data exchange and generated a model that generalized across heterogeneous, unharmonized datasets for prediction of clinical outcomes in patients with COVID-19, setting the stage for the broader use of FL in healthcare.

The pandemic has emphasized the need to expeditiously conduct data collaborations that empower the clinical and scientific communities when responding to rapidly evolving and widespread global challenges. Data sharing has ethical, regulatory and legal complexities that are underscored, and perhaps somewhat complicated, by the recent entrance of large technology companies into the healthcare data world15–17. A concrete example of these types of collaboration is our previous work on an AI-based SARS-COV-2 clinical decision support (CDS) model. This CDS model was developed at Mass General Brigham (MGB) and was validated across multiple health systems’ data. The inputs to the CDS model were chest X-ray (CXR) images, vital signs, demographic data and laboratory values that were shown in previous publications to be predictive of outcomes of patients with COVID-1918–21. CXR was selected as the imaging input because it is widely available and commonly indicated by guidelines such as those provided by ACR22, the Fleischner Society23, the WHO24, national thoracic societies25, national health ministry COVID handbooks and radiology societies across the world26. The output of the CDS model was a score, termed CORISK27, that corresponds to oxygen support requirements and that could aid in triaging patients

by frontline clinicians28–30. Healthcare providers have been known to prefer models that were validated on their own data27. To date most AI models, including the aforementioned CDS model, have been trained and validated on ‘narrow’ data that often lack diversity31,32, potentially resulting in overfitting and lower generalizability. This can be mitigated by training with diverse data from multiple sites without centralization of data33 using methods such as transfer learning34,35 or FL. FL is a method used to train AI models on disparate data sources, without the data being transported or exposed outside their original location. While applicable to many industries, FL has recently been proposed for cross-institutional healthcare research36. Federated learning supports the rapid launch of centrally orchestrated experiments with improved traceability of data and assessment of algorithmic changes and impact37. One approach to FL, called client-server, sends an ‘untrained’ model to other servers (‘nodes’) that conduct partial training tasks, in turn sending the results back to be merged in the central (‘federated’) server. This is conducted as an iterative process until training is complete36. Governance of data for FL is maintained locally, alleviating privacy concerns, with only model weights or gradients communicated between client sites and the federated server38,39. FL has already shown promise in recent medical imaging applications40–43, including in COVID-19 analysis8,44,45. A notable example is a
